subject: Business District Waste and Recycling Initiative
overview: City officials and consultants presented a new initiative to transition Medford businesses to private waste contracts and containerized disposal to improve cleanliness and rat control. The program mandates recycling compliance and the use of approved overflow bags or carts ahead of full enforcement in May 2025.

items.title: Introduction to the Squares Cleanliness Initiative
items.summary: Sal Di Stefano and Steve Smerdy introduced a city team and consultants tasked with implementing the 'Improving the Cleanliness of Our Squares' waste program.

items.title: Transition to Private Waste Responsibility
items.summary: Tim McGivern explained that new city contracts necessitate transitioning business districts from public waste disposal costs to private, fair-market arrangements.

items.title: New Overflow Bag and Hauler Requirements
items.summary: The city will require businesses still using bags to use green city-approved overflow bags starting January 1, 2025, and will mandate that all private haulers provide recycling services.

items.title: Implementation Timeline and Enforcement
items.summary: Jeremy Drake detailed a timeline including a new dumpster permitting process starting April 1, 2025, followed by full ordinance enforcement on May 1, 2025.

items.title: Technical Assistance for Small Businesses
items.summary: Heather Billings outlined free technical assistance available to help businesses evaluate waste volumes, select containers, and implement recycling or composting programs.

items.title: Square-Specific Meetings and Haines Square Pilot
items.summary: The city scheduled a series of Zoom meetings for individual business squares and discussed a pilot program for shared containers in Haines Square.

items.title: Q&A: Negotiated Rates and Service Eligibility
items.summary: Officials discussed negotiated rates for Waste Management services and clarified that businesses in buildings exceeding 2,500 square feet are generally ineligible for municipal collection.

items.title: Q&A: Public Health and Aesthetics
items.summary: Presenters addressed the initiative's benefits for rat control and litter reduction while considering ways to coordinate pickup days to minimize sidewalk clutter.
